sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Arakajú language' (stub): extinct Cariban language of Pará, extinct after 1820, Arakajú incorporated into the Aparai; cites Martius 1867, Kaufman 2007 (Wayana branch), Nimuendajú 1948, Gildea 2002; Croatian Wikipedia 'Arakajú jezik' repeats the Loukotka wordlist
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; no vocabulary or phonology beyond the seven Loukotka/Martius words.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p. 202 and comparative table (Karaib stock, Eastern languages).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry reads: 'Aracajú or Uaraguazú - extinct language mixed with many Tupi elements, once spoken on the Gurupatüba and Parú de Leste Rivers, Pará. [Martius 1867, vol. 2, pp. 17-18.]' plus a 13-word comparative table (head u-pupu, eye seresa, water tuna, fire uapto, sun chichi, moon yasüe, arrow uárapára, man apükaua) copied from Martius.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid arac1235 'Aracaju' (Unclassifiable, extinct); reference 79048 = Martius 1867, whose fullest description per Glottolog is only a wordlist, 3 pp., the only reference for NOCODE_Aracaju
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; confirms that Martius 1867 is the only descriptive reference (Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less).

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, II: Wörtersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Leipzig: Friedrich Fleischer. pp. 17-18 ('ARAQUAJÚ. Uara-guaçú, grosse Männer.')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The entire attestation is a ~50-item Latin-glossed wordlist (aqua tuna, ignis uapto, sol xixy, luna yasüe, homo apükaua, arcus coelestis uaimy uárapára, deus tupána..) with sporadic acute accents but no grammatical or phonological remark. Martius's general orthographic note (pp. 29-30, preface to the Tupi dictionary) says the acute accent 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' - a transcription convention, not a statement about Araquajú.

sources.citation: Kaufman, Terrence. 2007. South America. In C. Moseley, R. E. Asher & M. Darkes (eds.), Atlas of the World's Languages, 2nd ed., pp. 59-94. London: Routledge.
